title: Creating the best working environments for Civil Service in Greater Manchester

content.text: Greater Manchester and the Places for Growth programme

Greater Manchester is rapidly becoming a centre for digital and technology talent across government. It is a key location for the Civil Service’s Places for Growth programme which relocates thousands of roles outside of London.

With strong university links, a growing digital and technology workforce, and major government investment, including a new digital campus, Greater Manchester is a key location for creating opportunities for people to build careers in public service.

I'm a Data Analyst in Digital, Data and Technology based in our Greater Manchester offices, predominantly Trinity Bridge House. I also work as part of a committee to build a strong professional community, and most importantly offer our staff a sense of belonging.

If you’re looking to build a digital career in government outside London, our hub provides plenty of opportunities to grow and connect. Through a range of initiatives, we have made our community’s time in the office valuable and purpose-driven.
Trinity Bridge House

Trinity Bridge House is BIST’s main hub in Greater Manchester. It’s located right next to Salford Central train station, with our other sites positioned close to Manchester Piccadilly. All are within easy walking distance of the city centre. This gives colleagues quick access to Manchester’s shops, cafés and cultural scene, as well as excellent public transport links across the region.

Inside, the office is designed to support flexible, hybrid working. There are a variety of spaces to support both collaborative and focused individual work. Meeting rooms are equipped with high-quality technology for hybrid collaboration.

The building is shared with colleagues from HMRC and DESNZ, alongside dedicated areas for BIST teams. Our Manchester colleagues work across a wide range of roles; from technology and research to policy and logistics, collaborating closely with partners across the UK and internationally, including sector specialists and security experts.

How we create meaningful connections for our Manchester staff
Several clear insights emerged. Some of our findings are supported by research around hybrid working and employee expectations, while others reflect emerging insight from local experience.
Physical presence alone does not create connection
With hybrid and distributed teams, offices need to actively facilitate interaction and design opportunities for connection beyond physical proximity.
Inclusivity is critical to participation
Traditional formats, such as evening socials, unintentionally exclude some colleagues. Offering a wider range of formats significantly increases engagement.
Professional and social value are closely linked
Activities that combine skill development with networking, such as coding sessions or profession-specific meet-ups, are especially effective.
Place matters
Being part of a wider Manchester-based Civil Service community, rather than a single office, helps create a stronger sense of identity and shared purpose.
What this means for our Manchester staff

The Places for Growth initiative has created opportunities for digital professionals across the UK, with many Civil Service roles being available outside of London and reducing the need for people to relocate.
Using our insights we have focused on creating opportunities to build local networks outside of DBT and enable skill and experience sharing in our hubs.

Wider impact

Making roles available in more places widens the pool of applicants, helping the Civil Service attract and recruit stronger talent. The insights we’ve gained have broader implications for how the Civil Service approaches regional working. They suggest that investment in intentional cultural and community -building leads to greater collaboration and more attractive workplaces, especially outside of London.

More widely, it reinforces the idea that both hybrid working and regional distribution are cultural changes, not just logistical changes. Organisations that succeed are those that design environments people actively choose to engage with.
What comes next?
In Greater Manchester, the direction is towards a more connected and consolidated hub model, bringing teams closer together while maintaining flexibility.

Join a community in Manchester

With the rise of hybrid and distributed teams, the role of the office has changed permanently. In Greater Manchester we have shown that by providing more than a desk, we can transform the office from a workplace to a community.
By providing inclusive opportunities to connect, collaborate and learn, we can create places where people do their best work and feel part of something meaningful.
If you’re interested in being part of this journey, consider applying for roles in the Civil Service in Manchester.
